rq3_entries.value: The tool generates a ten-label candidate set for a person-selected span and can identify complete span–label pairs before annotation begins. (PDF p. 2)
quotes: "Our label recommendations surface a set of ten model-proposed labels after a user chooses a span of text to annotate." (p. 2)
"The pre-populated annotations suggest full sets of both text spans and corresponding labels." (p. 2)

rq3_entries.value: The person judges candidates, searches beyond inadequate recommendations, accepts or revises proposed pairs, and still identifies concepts the system omitted. (PDF pp. 2, 4)
quotes: "The user can choose to go with one of the recommendations or decide to search further." (p. 2)

"The user then can choose to accept this span and label combination in a single click on the green checkbox that appears as a dropdown; alternately, the user could choose to modify the label via the yellow pencil or to discard the result via the red ‘X’." (p. 4)

rq3_entries.value: yes — behavioral search choices measured whether users learned when the recommendations were inadequate. (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "Therefore, we see that their search patterns are closely aligned, and they generally learn to search further when necessary." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: gain — users generally developed a useful, though fallible, model of when to search beyond recommendations. (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "This indicates that users had a strong sense of cases in which the algorithm isn’t surfacing the correct answer." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: Search initiation differed between cases with and without the correct recommendation, measured across 18 clinicians over approximately eight hours each. (PDF pp. 2, 8)
quotes: "On ‘easy’ examples (those where a correct answer was in the recommendations), users in both the Standard mode and the Weakened mode only searched further 17% of the time and ultimately chose a recommended label 96% of the time." (p. 8)
"However, on ‘difficult’ examples, Standard users searched further 85% of the time and Weakened users 82% of the time." (p. 8)
"We analyze each annotator’s behavior and outcomes over approximately eight hours of annotation each, allowing us to account for effects over long time scales like tedium." (p. 2)

rq3_entries.value: author_measured — pre-population reduced self-initiated annotation without users recognizing the change. (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "Once again, this loss of agency was not correlated with users’ prior accuracy and, qualitatively, users did not recognize it was happening." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: no — the implemented support does not withdraw as competence grows.
not_applicable
Users must judge and revise proposed labels and identify unsuggested spans; this responsibility does not decrease with improvement. (PDF pp. 4, 10)
quotes: "At any time, the user can return to edit any annotation by clicking on its surrounding box." (p. 4)
"While users with pre-populated suggestions overall had slightly higher total recall than users without, they initiated the creation of fewer additional annotations." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: repeated_n_sessions (2 stages) — live and asynchronous annotation work occurred across a two-stage study. (PDF pp. 2, 7)
quotes: "We run a two-stage user study on 18 clinicians from 9 different United States medical institutions, in which we artificially vary the extent and accuracy of both of the aforementioned decision aids." (p. 2)
"Each user annotated the first note of each stage live over Zoom, talking out loud, and then annotated their next two notes asynchronously, with screen recording." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: Pre-populated suggestions caused clinicians to lose critical engagement and add fewer new annotations without realizing it. (PDF p. 12)
quotes: "Without them realizing it, the presence of pre-populated suggestions leads them to lose critical engagement in the task and add fewer new annotations than each had previously." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: performance
empirical
mixed_factorial — recommendation/suggestion mode and task difficulty were varied, with comparisons across stages. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Our study had a multiple factor design, where we evaluated the performance of users (i) across different recommendation modes and (ii) across different annotation task difficulties that naturally arose in the task." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: 18 — the same clinician cohort completed both stages. (PDF pp. 6, 9)
quotes: "We recruited 18 clinicians via Twitter and email lists." (p. 6)
"The same 18 clinicians participated in this stage of the study, and they spent approximately three hours each on this stage of the study." (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: mixed — the cohort combined medical-school graduates with third- and fourth-year medical students. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "Our users (8 men, 10 women) consisted of 4 medical school graduates, 6 fourth years, and 8 third years;" (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: control_condition — Stage 1 included a no-recommendation mode and Stage 2 included a no-suggestion mode. (PDF pp. 7, 9)
quotes: "First, users were assigned randomly to one of three modes: the None mode, with no recommendations (5 users), the Standard recommendation mode (6 users), or the Weakened recommendation mode (7 users)." (p. 7)

"They were now re-assigned randomly to one of four modes: the No suggestion mode (3 users), the Standard suggestion mode (4 users), the Augmented suggested mode (5 users), and the Weakened suggestion mode (5 users)." (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: test_only — the paper reports named tests and p-values but no standardized effect size. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "We find that total recall is significantly affected by mode (p<0.03), annotation difficulty (p<1e-16), and their interactions (p<1e-4)." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: approximately eight hours of annotation per clinician across two stages. (PDF p. 2)
quotes: "We analyze each annotator’s behavior and outcomes over approximately eight hours of annotation each, allowing us to account for effects over long time scales like tedium." (p. 2)

claim_entries.value: Standard recommendations did not significantly improve total recall over no recommendations; confidence indicators did not measurably improve error handling. (PDF pp. 7, 9)
quotes: "The superiority of the Standard mode over the None mode is not statistically significant, but results indicate that the presence of recommendations does not decrease recall, a prior worry." (p. 7)

"Further, the presence of the confidence indicators in the Augmented mode did not make any noticeable impact on user’s rate of modifying incorrectly suggested labels or their accuracy on the low-confidence subset." (p. 9)

claim_entries.value: evidence_supports_claim

Logged behavior and within-person stage comparisons support the claim for this clinician sample: suggestion users' nontrivial recall fell by 12% on average while the stage-by-mode interaction was significant. (PDF p. 10)
quotes: "Users without suggestions increased on average 4% between the two stages, indicating Stage 2 may have been slightly easier, but users with suggestions dropped on average 12%." (p. 10)

"In an Aligned Rank transform test with factors of (i) stage and (ii) whether users received pre-annotations, there was a statistically significant effect of stage (p<0.005) and of the interaction between stage and mode (p=0.01)." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: clinical concept annotation in electronic health notes. (PDF p. 1)
quotes: "In this work, we use a clinical text annotation task to study whether for domain experts, their expertise mediates their interactions with automation." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support reduces search and annotation burden during the current task. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "Recommendations could decrease the burden of the user searching over the large label space, especially since algorithms could present a correct label over 80% of the time [28]." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: expert_or_professional — users were selected for substantial medical training and clinical-note experience. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "To ensure a consistent and sufficient clinical background, we required users to have completed at least two years of medical school and to have experience with clinical notes in United States healthcare settings." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: not_applicable — control participants completed the same annotation work; the support addressed burden and efficiency rather than an inability to perform it.
process — the study measured speed and user actions such as search. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "We analyze several dependent variables: users’ accuracy, the speed of clinical annotation, and the actions taken in the platform (e.g. choosing to search)." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — span recall, total recall, and label accuracy assessed the produced annotations. (PDF p. 7)
quotes: "Accuracy was evaluated via span recall, the proportion of annotations in the gold standard that users annotated the span for, total recall, the proportion of annotations in the gold standard that users got the correct span and correct label for, and label accuracy, the percentage of time users chose a correct label for a set of spans." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: learning_or_transfer — search behavior measured whether users learned when to override recommendations. (PDF p. 8)
quotes: "Therefore, we see that their search patterns are closely aligned, and they generally learn to search further when necessary." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — recommendations and pre-population organize the task into explicit candidate labels and span–label pairs. (PDF p. 2)
quotes: "We introduce a new text annotation system that provides two major forms of automated decision support: label recommendations for mapping spans to concepts, and fully pre-populated annotation suggestions." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — the recommendation display responds to the span the user has just selected. (PDF p. 5)
quotes: "As a result, our system surfaces recommendations automatically on the right label panel when a user highlights a span, as seen in Figure 2(a, c)." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — tutorial feedback makes discrepancies between the user's output and the gold standard explicit. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "Underneath, it iterates through all the annotations, providing a description of the differences between the gold standard and the user output, if any." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — the recommendations use classical NLP information retrieval, while pre-population can use clinical concept-extraction systems. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "In our studies, we use the recommendation algorithm detailed in Agrawal et al., which draws on classical information retrieval techniques from NLP [1]." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the scaffold meaning comes from information-retrieval and clinical extraction algorithms rather than a language model. (PDF p. 6)
quotes: "Possible existing concept extraction systems include cTAKES, MetaMap, MedLEE, and scispaCy [2, 10, 32, 42]." (p. 6)

limitations: "Other limitations include the low-stakes setting of our study task." (p. 11)
"Since we did not deploy in a live setting, and there was no consequence for incorrect actions, users may not have been as careful as they would have been under greater pressure." (p. 11)
"Additionally, we found that presenting model confidence had little-to-no-impact, and users admitted to not using the confidence flags." (p. 11)
"Other UI techniques might have made these confidences more salient to users." (p. 11)
boundary_conditions: "The clinical text annotation task involves a rich set of subtasks and decisions that allowed us to probe questions of trust and agency in expert decision makers." (p. 11)
"However, our findings do not necessarily extend to simpler settings." (p. 11)

"To ensure a consistent and sufficient clinical background, we required users to have completed at least two years of medical school and to have experience with clinical notes in United States healthcare settings." (p. 6)

the controlled mixed-factorial comparisons support the bounded claim about perceived understandability in the tested loan and music explanation tasks, without establishing learning or deployed-use effects (PDF pp. 5, 9).
quotes: "In a user study, participants evaluated the understandability of explanations for different framing and labeling conditions for loan applications and music recommendations." (p. 2)
"Our empirical contribution has highlighted the added value of positive framing and (positive) semantic labeling in aiding AI understandability." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: interpreting local AI decision explanations for loan eligibility and music recommendation (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "In the loan application domain, participants were required to interpret explanations of a loan application prediction system." (p. 5)
"An explanation showed why the prediction was made based on the audio features of the song and their similarity to the selected profile." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support helps users interpret current algorithmic suggestions (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "We discuss two adaptations that can improve the users’ understanding of algorithmic suggestions." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: novice_or_learner — the evaluation used lay participants and the design targets people without technical interpretation expertise (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "We tested these two improvements in a user study where we show explanations with and without these potential improvements to (lay) participants." (p. 3)

"The explanations that the tools provide should be as clear as possible, given that one cannot count on the fact that the user is tech-savvy enough to figure out what the technical output conveys." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: knowledge_or_concept_gap — users may not know how a numeric or bar contribution maps to a domain outcome (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "However, interpretation of those values requires that users make an additional cognitive step to understand what these values or bars imply." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measured perceived understanding while participants interpreted explanations (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Participants interpreted the explanations and rated their understandability." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the interface organizes feature contributions as a case-specific list and visualization with explicit direction cues (PDF pp. 3, 6).
quotes: "The generated explanation is in the format of a feature-importance list and a visualization." (p. 3)
"The primary component is the list visualizer from the ArgueView-package (Figure 3)." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — LIME and Shap derive case-specific feature contributions from surrogate models; no generative model produces the scaffold’s meaning (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "LIME is a model-agnostic explanation tool developed by Ribeiro, Singh, and Guestrin [25]. It generates its explanations using a surrogate linear model and proximity sampling." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the support path is conventional model-agnostic XAI based on surrogate models rather than a language or foundation model (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "To explain the output for a certain set of inputs, the model-agnostic interpretability tools typically construct a simpler surrogate model by sampling the original (black-box) model near the inputs of interest, and then offering an explanation based on this simpler model." (p. 3)

limitations: "Our study has several limitations. First, the decisions had a limited direct importance to the participants." (p. 9)
"The loan applications were for imaginary people with no relation to the participant, hence participants might have been indifferent to the actual prediction." (p. 9)

"Similarly, in the music domain, though the predictions were personalized based on their preferred genre, there was no consequence for the participant to whether the prediction was positive or negative." (p. 9)
"Another issue is that we presented participants with 24 trials which might have caused some learning effects or decreased attention during the trial." (p. 9)
"Then again, the entire study did not take longer than 20-25 minutes and our randomization of domains and conditions balances any effects of fatigue on our data." (p. 9)
"Several trials were deleted because of coding error in the visualizations that were shown." (p. 6)
boundary_conditions: "We focus on these model-agnostic interpretable AI tools that use surrogate models and their functionality towards explaining singular decisions." (p. 3)
"Positive framing should of course only be used in situations where there is a decision-class that users value positively as it might otherwise backfire." (p. 9)
"It is also complicated to have the software automatically deduce which decision-class is the positive one." (p. 9)
"Additionally, frequent users of interpretation tools may have come to expect positive contributions to imply positive contribution to the decision-class." (p. 9)
"It can be used in conjunction with LIME and Shap to generated explanations with adjustable contribution framing and contribution labels." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: interactive vehicle-routing optimisation and decision support — the exemplar is VRPTW work (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "As our exemplar we chose to develop a tool for solving the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW), a variation of the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — support is used to solve routing instances during the session (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Participants were then asked to solve an optimisation problem in four different scenarios." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: novice_or_learner — users were selected for lacking optimisation expertise (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "As end-users of interactive optimisation tool are more likely to be non-experts rather than optimisation experts, we only selected participants who did not have computer science or optimisation expertise." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: evaluation_or_judgment_gap — without understandable solution and constraint representations, users cannot readily assess alternatives or guide refinement (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Evaluating/Comparing solutions and Guiding the solver will be very difficult" (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: process — interaction use and participant strategies were observed (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Fig. 6 (right) shows the number of participants who used various features of the interface in each scenario and Fig. 6 (middle) summarises participants response to the questions about the system interface." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — produced route solutions were assessed for improvement and optimality (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "8 out of 10 participants developed a better solution in Part 1." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the schedule organises customers by truck and planned service progression (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Customer lines are grouped by the truck which services them." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the representation makes infeasibility visible instead of hiding it (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "Second, it visually distinguishes valid from invalid situations." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — feedback responds immediately to a user’s edit (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "All participants agreed that it was necessary to provide such immediate feedback when changes are made." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — constraints, manual edits, and re-optimisation let the tool address unanticipated scenarios (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "flexibly handle a variety of scenarios" (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — the person and optimisation solver share the refinement work (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Re-optimise allows the user to collaboratively solve an optimisation problem with the optimisation solver with the control of when and what to re-optimise." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: non_generative_ai — a constraint-programming optimisation engine generates and revises candidate routes (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We implemented our test system as a web application, with the back-end optimisation based on the MiniZinc [41] system and the Gecode [51] constraint programming solver." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_llm_ai — the semantic outputs come from a constraint-programming solver rather than a foundation model (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We implemented our test system as a web application, with the back-end optimisation based on the MiniZinc [41] system and the Gecode [51] constraint programming solver." (p. 5)
